summary: One Blocker: FR-1 adds a `loops` approval part with a draft default, but the published check (checks.ts) iterates every approval part except `print`, so the accepted FAIL message of st2/1 changes at Phase 1 Green. FR-1 also says the message does not change. Two commitments contradict; the implementer must choose. Four Major findings: the loops-minutes rule requires periodMinutes 30 while FR-8 applies the checks to Levels 3 and 4 (49-minute periods); the FR-6 recall rule cites taughtTo, which holds only graphemes and tricky words, so frame and word cards cannot pass; the ownership section omits the same-file serialization rule for the print track overlap; the approved `loops` record has no named enforcement of date and words. Three Nits. Reuse, placement, dates, gates, done-when lines, the byte-equal proof guard, the warn-to-fail switch, and the no-pnpm rule check out.

paraphrase.proposes: The track adds five teaching routines from research item A-42 to the Storytime Level 2 weeks: an oral blend drill on step A4, a correct-practise-retest loop on the sound steps A1 to A3, a fast-way sight-word step with a timed check on A6 and D2, a fixed set of three questions on each read-along, and a daily recall of five cards in the opening. New optional schema fields carry the routines. Six new checks gate them with the status warn until the content of weeks 1 to 8 lands, then fail. The teacher manual prints the routines only with the new `--loops` option, so the approved week 1 proof of 2026-11-05 stays byte-equal. The day stays 30 minutes: the loops take minutes from the donor steps, and Daniel approves the English and Thai text before the release proof of 2026-11-20.
paraphrase.current_system: A week file holds meta, focus, books, song, five daily scripts with steps, review strips, the Friday check, and approvals (schema.ts). checkStorytimeWeek (checks.ts) runs rules for minutes, books, decodability, Thai, and review strips; check-weeks.ts prints the reports per level. One accepted FAIL exists: the published row of st2/1, because the images, audio, and song parts are draft; the published check iterates every approval part except `print`. manual.ts renders the teacher book HTML from the week; compileStorytimeManual takes the language and the paper, and the two print scripts build the Thai teacher book PDF. The opening is a fixed 6-minute routine, and the recall of a day prints the moved steps of the day before.

blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] spec FR-1 (approval part `loops`): FR-1 adds `StorytimeApprovalsSchema.loops` with the default draft, but FR-1 also says "The `published` check and its message do not change" and the acceptance says the message of st2/1 stays as at the baseline. The published check (dashboard/lib/storytime/checks.ts lines 320-325) iterates every approval part except `print`, so the new draft part adds "loops not approved" to the detail of the accepted FAIL of st2/1 (the print track plan, Green 2 evidence, records the detail `images not approved; audio not approved; song not approved`). The message changes at Phase 1 Green, or the published check code changes, which FR-1 forbids. The spec must pick one: exclude `loops` in the published check like `print`, or drop the message criterion. Rationale: two acceptance criteria cannot both hold; the choice changes code.
nonblocking_findings: F2 [Major] spec FR-7 + FR-8: the `loops-minutes` acceptance requires `periodMinutes` is 30, but FR-8 applies the checks to Levels 2 to 4, and a Level 3 or 4 week has `periodMinutes` 49 (schema.ts lines 73-74). After the Phase 3 switch, every Level 3 or 4 week fails `loops-minutes`. The check must compare against `meta.periodMinutes`, or skip weeks outside the 30-minute periods. Rationale: the check scope and the check rule contradict.

F3 [Major] spec FR-6: Comprehension gap: the rule "the item text is in the taught set of that week (`taughtTo`)" is undefined for the recall kinds `frame` and `word`, which FR-6 allows. `taughtTo` (dashboard/lib/storytime/checks.ts lines 54-63) holds only the taught graphemes, the tricky words, and the program week. A frame sentence or a family word is not in that set, so `loops-recall` as written rejects every `frame` and `word` recall item. The spec must define the taught set for each card kind. Rationale: an undefined project-specific term that decides the check result.

F4 [Major] spec Ownership and overlap: the week_package paragraph states the rule "The orchestrator runs no task of the two tracks at the same time on one file", but the print track paragraph does not. This track edits `make-teacher-book-print.ts`, `manual.ts`, and `i18n.ts` in Phase 2 (2026-11-05 to 11-07), while the print track builds the week 1 proof in its Phase 6 (2026-11-05 to 11-09) and the release proof in its Phase 9 (2026-11-19 to 11-25) from the same files. The spec must state the same serialization rule for this overlap. Rationale: two active tracks can edit one owned file at the same time.

F5 [Major] spec FR-1 + FR-11: FR-11 says the approved `loops` record has his words and the date, but the app-part shape (`StorytimeAppApprovalSchema`, schema.ts lines 458-461) leaves `date` and `words` optional, and unlike the print part (schema.ts lines 445-450) it has no refine. The spec does not say whether the schema or a loop check refuses an approved `loops` part without the date or the words. Rationale: an edge-case behavior that the plan leaves open, and the consent record (anti-pattern A2) depends on it.

F6 [Nit] spec Terms (Donor step): the donor list names "the opening", but D7 keeps the opening at 6 minutes, and FR-7 reads the opening minutes from `meta.openingMinutes`, which `loopMinutes` cannot change. The opening can never donate minutes. Rationale: a definition that D7 overrides; it does not change what the implementer builds.

F7 [Nit] plan Phase 3 Red: the byte-equality test compares the hash of the baseline file with the shipped week "with the new fields removed", but the plan does not name the removal operation. Parse, delete the FR-1 fields, and re-serialize with the original formatting, or the hash differs. Rationale: a test-mechanics detail; the test itself catches a wrong choice.

F8 [Nit] spec FR-12 vs plan: FR-12 says three messages to the PM session, but the plan sends five (Hand-off 1, the page-count note, Hand-off 2 pin, Hand-off 3 --loops notice, the report). Rationale: a count mismatch in prose; the plan is the superset and the PM confirmations cover all five.

F9 [Nit] plan Phase 2 Green: the new Thai headings in `i18n.ts` get no named Daniel check, although the NFR says every new English line needs his Thai check. They surface first in the release proof, which Daniel approves on 2026-11-24 in the print track. Rationale: a coverage note; no build change.
